b1.summary: Every run fixed the reported crossing (a post riding into a reversal), multi-marker headers and the injected erase gate. They failed on two traps: the custody stamp carrying the enclosing act instead of the act performed (5/6 runs), and the injected amendment fallback that lets the original's marker authorise its amended copy (5/6). All are security misses. All 296 functional tests passed in every run.

b2.note: No single test fails in every run. Each test is the only failure of one run (the cascade test for DeepSeek run 3, the amendment test for MiMo run 1), so dropping either one turns one model into 1/3.

b4.note: Four runs fail both traps, and each of the other two fails one of them.

b5.open_human_question: NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW: YES on the decisive cascade test: 'confirm test 2's custody reading: "only with that act's own authority" versus "never survives into an act other than the one that carried it"'. FAIRNESS also lists five 'Required: generalize' rewrites (the posting/reversing/erasing list, the X-Pacioli-Consent header, the POST example, 'an empty entry is never a marker', the lifecycle sentence), and none of them is applied to instruction.md.

b6.reason: The cascade/custody trap is covered by the upstream fix f3c7219 (guard 0.10.0). _CONSENT_ESTABLISHED now carries the act, and the CHANGELOG lists the mutation 'propagating the act a nested write RODE instead of the act it performed' as tested. The amendment fallback in enforce.py is injected and not upstream, so it is uncovered. DeepSeek run 3 is decided only by the covered trap.

quotes: never carries to a document the authorised act did not create
never survives into an act other than the one that carried it. That holds however deeply an act is nested and whatever a request body names.
may present more than one marker in the consent header, separated by whitespace or commas ... an empty entry is never a marker
posting it, reversing it, or erasing it
b7.note: Each decisive trap is paraphrased as a rule. The fairness reviewer's required generalisations were not applied.

b8.gate: .sound (oracle passes; 438 project tests OK on the injected tree and on the reference)
b8.note: alternative_fix.patch and hardening.patch pass. 11 wrong-fix checks are caught.

c1.mechanism: authorization: binding of a consent marker to the act and document across nested lifecycle acts (confused deputy / authority carried across cascades)
c1.domain: accounting ERP API capability guard (Pacioli Guard)

c2.pattern: missed nested propagation (authority carried at second level) + missed relationship fallback
c2.note: Custody is real code that the upstream fix changes, at a site far from the reported one-line predicate. The amendment fallback is planted.

d2.evidence: Both injected sites copy the repo's own long, version-stamped docstring voice and give product reasons. The code is natural: a one-step amended_from lookup, and a DELETE act added to the cancel ride branch. But they claim 'Added 0.9.6' and '(0.9.3)' histories that the in-repo CHANGELOG at the pin (which records every release in detail) never mentions. The amendment docstring also spells out the exact fallback ('its marker is presented to the pure core as the marker for this document'). The injection edits the project's own test_act.py to register on_trash as well.

e2.why: All 6 runs are trusted, all at medium confidence, none high.

e3.why: READY, but NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW: YES is open on the decisive cascade test, and the required generalisations were never applied.

e4.why: Both decisive tests catch an act or document that proceeds without consent.

e5.why: Partly: the amendment trap is uncovered, but the cascade trap is covered by upstream 0.10.0 and alone decides DeepSeek run 3.

concerns: The human-review question on the decisive cascade test is open.
FAIRNESS 'Required: generalize' items were not applied, and the instruction states each trap almost as a rule (leaky).
The upstream fix covers the custody trap, so with an upstream lookup DeepSeek likely drops to 1/3 or worse.
Each decisive test is the sole failure of one run, so the margin is thin (two runs at 0.875).
The injected docstrings claim release history the CHANGELOG does not show (forensic tell).
All audits are medium confidence: no final code or transcript.
one_line: Frappe consent guard: models stop a post from riding into a reversal, but miss that a cascade must carry the act it performed, and miss a planted amendment fallback that lets one document's marker authorise its copy.
